# Paths TruffleHog does not scan.
#
# Scope: test fixtures and nothing else. A negative test for a credential-handling
# path has to contain something that looks like a credential — `https://user:pw@host`,
# a fake `postgres://user:pw@host` DSN, a placeholder token — and the case under test
# is that the code refuses it. Those literals are unverifiable by construction, and
# they are the only findings this file exists to silence.
#
# Production code is deliberately NOT excluded, and neither are the integration and
# end-to-end suites, which carry real credentials (`OPENTAG_JWT_SECRET`,
# `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`) through `.env` files and workflow variables. A scanner that
# skipped those would be silent exactly where a leak would matter.
#
# One pattern per line, as a regular expression matched against the path. The `__tests__`
# directory and the `.test.`/`.spec.` filename conventions are asserted by the tests in
# this repository, so these two forms cover every test file there is.
__tests__/
\.test\.[cm]?tsx?$
\.spec\.[cm]?tsx?$
